When every spreadsheet tells a different supply-chain story

Conflicting reports are evidence about definitions, ownership and the way decisions are made.

Illustrative scenario analysis · 6–8 minute read
This article illustrates a recurring supply-chain pattern and the JourneyIQ Supply Chain Diagnostic method. It does not describe a named client, completed engagement or verified customer outcome.

The situation

Procurement, planning, logistics and finance each have a legitimate file, but the weekly meeting becomes a reconciliation exercise.

Treat disagreement as evidence

Different totals often reveal different units, dates, identifiers and definitions of availability. Those differences determine what the business is actually measuring.

Create a common journey

Define the minimum event model, preserve source references and distinguish blocking errors from warnings and caveats.

A decision contract

Shared definitions clarify which evidence starts an escalation, who owns the exception and which change is material enough to review.
